name: Windrose
notes: Friends join with the invite code the server prints in its log ('Server Connection Info') and writes to R5\ServerDescription.json (InviteCode). By default it opens no ports at all (P2P through Windrose's connection service), so the port 7777 entries only matter with UseDirectConnection=true (DirectConnectionServerPort, TCP and UDP). ServerDescription.json (UTF-8, CRLF) is in R5\, written on the first start; each world's gameplay settings are WorldDescription.json under R5\Saved\SaveProfiles\Default\RocksDB_v2\<version>\Worlds\<world id>\. Stop the server before editing either file (the install's DedicatedServer.md lists the fields). Basecamp starts the Shipping exe with -log, as the developers' StartServerForeground.bat does: WindroseServer.exe and the Shipping exe are Windows GUI programs, and only -log gives the server a console that Ctrl+Break can reach. On Ctrl+Break it logs 'Engine exit requested (reason: ConsoleCtrl RequestExit)', syncs its backups ('Finished sync backups. Result true') and exits, with exit code 0xC000013A even so. Without -log the stop can only be a kill. -log also shows that console as a window on the desktop of whoever is logged in; under Basecamp's startup task nobody sees it. Worlds are RocksDB folders, with zipped copies in R5\Saved\SaveProfiles\Default\RocksDB_v2_Backups\. The working folder must be the install folder, or the log file isn't found.
